title: fix: repair legacy config during same-version updates
body:
Related: #188694

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `openclaw update` refusing an already-current npm installation with legacy config that Doctor can repair, unless the operator also supplied `--channel`.

## User Impact

A plain same-version update can repair supported legacy settings, such as `gateway.bind: "localhost"`, and continue maintenance. The normal config writer preserves the original backup. Unknown fields still fail with actionable Doctor guidance; foreign profiles retain their ownership checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Already-current updates skip candidate admission. Prepare the existing source-bound Doctor plan for the selected maintenance config before installed admission, then let the existing finalizer persist it. This reconnects the repair owner without bypassing validation or introducing options, state, or schema changes.

The masked report does not establish that its five rejected fields match this reproduction. Release 2026.10.9 still accepts `agents.defaults.heartbeat`; main's later heartbeat retirement uses a separate stateful Doctor migration and is outside this config-only repair. Related rather than closing the issue.

## Evidence

- RED on pinned main `81cf32d99769`: the real update command with file-backed config and the actual Doctor planner/writer exits 1 for a same-version no-channel update; the explicit-channel sibling passes.
- GREEN with the fix: four focused cases passed, covering no-channel and explicit-channel repair, byte-for-byte original config backup, unknown-key refusal with unchanged input and Doctor guidance, and foreign-profile ownership. Final wrapper wall time 77.08s, including cold worker preparation; test-file time 39.09s. Package-manager/service adapters are fixed fixtures; this is owning-command integration proof.
- Existing candidate/installed admission controls: 15 selected tests passed, including heartbeat projection and invalid config controls (52.41s wrapper).
- Targeted owner/test typecheck, typed lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview (medium, P0–P2), complete local diff against `81cf32d99769` plus unchanged owner/fixture context: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The reviewer could not execute tests in its empty sandbox. pr-simplify retained the existing planner/writer; production +14/-2 lines, net test growth 34 lines with a separate 34-line allocation for the regression and negative control. The +34 allocation matches measured growth; terminal CI classification follows.

Installed-package proof now passes on Linux x64 / Node 26.12.1 through the real installed CLI, using `openclaw update --no-restart --yes --json` without a channel or tag:

| Installed package | Result | Config and backup |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Published npm 2026.10.9 | RED: exit 1, `invalid-config`; current and registry target both 2026.10.9 | Original bytes unchanged |
| Candidate from exact `0c0d540cc23876d33d4ee977ccaab7f38925dd7d`, installed over that npm prefix | GREEN: exit 0, `status: ok`; current and target both 2026.10.9 | `gateway.bind: localhost` becomes `loopback`; `agents.defaults.pdfMaxBytesMb: 23` becomes `pdfMaxMb: 23`; canonical `.bak` equals the original bytes |
| Same candidate, plus `unknownSetting: true` | Exit 1, `invalid-config`, actionable `openclaw doctor --fix` guidance | Input bytes unchanged |

The original and successful canonical-backup SHA-256 are both `f0bd909915af582cb8e48aa3a41604aa47b0767607c4f9f03d00391cd760aff0`. The candidate retained its exact `0c0d540` build identity after update. Its canonical package build and tarball integrity check passed, using a pinned source archive and a private copy of the worktree dependencies verified against the frozen lock. The registry's actual `latest` was 2026.10.9; the source package already declares 2026.10.9. No version edit, registry stub, package-target override, or admission bypass arranged equality.

Fixture prerequisite: the newly created published state needed main's existing client-credential custody migration before the positive update case could run. The existing credential-only `doctor --client-credentials --fix --non-interactive --json` succeeded in the disposable profile. A temporarily valid config selected the local engine; that command left its config bytes unchanged. The exact original legacy bytes were restored before update. No legacy-config Doctor repair was run as preparation. The final GREEN and negative control used that same prepared state. GREEN took 16.185s; the negative control took 16.341s. This proves the config repair and backup contract, not migration of arbitrary real user databases.

All mutable files stayed in the proof directory, with isolated HOME, npm prefix/cache, XDG directories, state/config selectors, and temp storage. Final runs used unprivileged filesystem namespaces and Landlock to hide protected host trees and service sockets, deny service executables and TCP binds, and keep normal CLI logic intact. Their syscall audits show zero successful protected-file accesses, service-command executions, or TCP binds. No Gateway started. An initial HOME-only attempt unexpectedly executed service diagnostics, inspected the host installation, and appended to a shared temp log; it is excluded from proof and documented in the local report. Intermediate temp/process-identity and credential-custody setup failures are also excluded. No further Podman or Testbox attempt was made.

macOS arm64 and the reporter's exact masked fields remain unverified. The PR is mergeable, so no rebase was needed; source and the prior independent review remain unchanged.

The first full-file local attempt passed 14 cases but its wrapper rejected changed input bytes during formatting; the frozen full-file rerun timed out on the loaded host after 12 passing cases. Only the final frozen four-case run above is claimed as final touched-contract proof. No issue comment, release, live Gateway change, prepare, or merge.

Exact-head CI [41132188644](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41132188644) reached terminal **failure** on unchanged head `0c0d540cc23876d33d4ee977ccaab7f38925dd7d`. Changed Node tests, type checks, lint, and all three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed. The only underlying failure was [baseline ratchets / test-lines](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41132188644/job/124326182429): total 6,310,666, ceiling 6,309,597, overage 1,069, net growth +34. The +34 allocation matches this PR's +34 lines, leaving the base's absolute debt unchanged. The aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` also failed because of that ratchet result; the other executed checks passed.

Base evidence is qualified: the exact prepared base's [push run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41129974074) skipped this job after a security-fast failure. The [current hourly main ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41130962529/job/124321849014) explicitly reports 1,041 lines of existing ceiling debt and passes only because its net growth is zero. The automatic classifier calls the PR failure new because that main job passed; manual inspection shows positive growth exposing existing ceiling debt, with no new allocation deficit. This is not a same-exit baseline match or a passing gate. No allocation enlargement, scalar change, unrelated test deletion, ignore, rebase, prepare, or merge was performed.

The maintainer accepted this inherited-debt exception at 22:06Z (same precedent as #188560). The ratchet and aggregate gate remain red; no budgets, ignores, or tests were changed for that failure. The existing hosted review has no code findings; its posted installed-CLI proof hold predates the evidence above. No fresh hosted review was requested.
